question: A 29-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 3-day history of a swollen right knee. Over the past several weeks, he has had similar episodes affecting the right knee and sometimes also the left elbow, in which the swelling lasted an average of 5 days. He has a history of a rash that subsided 2 months ago. He lives in Connecticut with his wife and works as a landscaper. His temperature is 37.8°C (100°F), pulse is 90/min, respirations are 12/min, and blood pressure is 110/75 mm Hg. Physical examination shows a tender and warm right knee; range of motion is limited by pain. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. His hematocrit is 44%, leukocyte count is 10,300/mm3, and platelet count is 145,000/mm3. Serum electrolyte concentrations are within normal limits. Arthrocentesis is performed and the synovial fluid is cloudy. Gram stain is negative. Analysis of the synovial fluid shows a leukocyte count of 70,000/mm3 and 80% neutrophils. Serologic testing confirms the diagnosis. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: History of recurrent joint swelling -> History of rash -> Serologic testing confirms the diagnosis -> 80% CHAIN: Swollen right knee with warm and tender joint -> Limited range of motion due to pain -> Synovial fluid analysis shows high leukocyte count and neutrophils -> 85% CHAIN: Cloudy synovial fluid -> Gram stain negative -> Leukocyte count of 70,000/mm3 with 80% neutrophils -> 90% CHAIN: Synovial fluid analysis consistent with septic arthritis -> Serologic testing confirms the diagnosis -> 95% CHAIN: Location in Connecticut -> Outdoor occupation as a landscaper -> Possible exposure to infectious agents -> 80%
enhanced_information: The most likely cause of the patient's symptoms is Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection, supported by the history of recurrent joint swelling, serologic testing confirming the diagnosis, and synovial fluid analysis showing high leukocyte count and neutrophils. The evidence paths related to pain, joint tenderness, and arthritis do not provide additional relevant information in this context.
analysis: The patient's presentation with recurrent joint swelling, synovial fluid analysis showing high leukocyte count and neutrophils, and serologic testing confirming the diagnosis point towards a likely Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection. The history of a rash that subsided 2 months ago could be related to disseminated gonococcal infection. The absence of other findings like erosions or deformities typical of chronic arthritis makes Neisseria gonorrhoeae the most likely cause.
